Maze rules and algorithm conventions

The 47-cell maze matches Lectures 1–4. Each move earns −1, including a move into the goal. Hitting a wall or boundary leaves the state unchanged. Goal 8 is absorbing, earns zero thereafter, and always has value zero. β = 0.9. Initial arrows are one reproducible random deterministic policy (seed 42).

VFI: improve the policy, then perform one simultaneous evaluation sweep. PFI: fully evaluate the current policy by a linear solve, then improve it. GPI / MPI: improve the policy, then perform k simultaneous evaluation sweeps. Generalized policy iteration is the broader framework; the finite-k algorithm here is modified policy iteration.

All action comparisons use the same value array. Retain the current action when it is tied for best; otherwise use up, down, left, right order. The goal action is immaterial. VFI and MPI stop when the Bellman residual is below 10⁻¹⁰, then return a greedy policy. PFI stops when improvement changes no action after full evaluation. Displayed numbers are rounded; the calculation uses full precision.

One evaluation sweep and one linear solve have different costs. The frame counts are not runtime comparisons. All methods converge to the same values but may select different shortest routes. A looping policy has value −1/(1−β) = −10. For a shortest route of d moves, V* = −(1−βd)/(1−β).
